The virgins said to me, “The shepherd is not coming here today.” “What, then, shall I do?” I said. “Wait for him until late,” they said.[a] “If he comes, he will speak with you. If he does not come, you will stay here with us until he comes.”

2. I said to them, “I will wait for him until late. But if he does not come, I will go home and return in the morning.” They replied, “You have been entrusted to us. You cannot leave us.”

3. “Where, then, will I stay?” I said. “You will sleep with us as a brother, not as a husband,” they said. “You are our brother, and from now on we are going to live with you, for we love you very much.” I was embarrassed to stay with them.

4. The one who seemed to be first among them began kissing and embracing me.[b] When the others saw her embracing me, they too began kissing me, leading me around the tower and playing with me.

5. I felt as though I had become younger, and I too began playing with them. Some danced in a chorus, others danced, and others sang.[c] I walked silently with them around the tower and was glad to be with them.

6. When evening came, I wanted to go home. But they would not let me; they kept me there. I stayed with them that night and slept beside the tower.

7. The virgins spread their linen tunics on the ground and had me lie down in their midst. They did nothing at all except pray. I too prayed with them continually, no less than they did. The virgins rejoiced to see me praying like this. I remained there with them until the second hour of the next day.[d]

8. Then the shepherd arrived and said to the virgins, “Have you done him any harm?” “Ask him,” they said. I said to him, “Sir, I was glad to stay with them.” “What did you have for supper?” he said. “Sir,” I said, “I feasted on the Lord’s words all night.” “Did they receive you well?” he said. “Yes, sir,” I said.

9. “Now,” he said, “what do you want to hear first?” “Sir,” I said, “just as you showed me things from the beginning, I ask you to explain them as I ask you about them.” “As you wish,” he said. “I will explain them to you and hide nothing at all from you.”

translation:
  text: 'The virgins told me, “The shepherd will not come here today.” I asked, “What shall I do?” They
    said, “Wait until late.[a] If he comes, he will speak with you. If not, stay here with us until he
    comes.”


    2. I said, “I will wait until late. If he does not come, I will go home and return in the morning.”
    They replied, “You were entrusted to us. You cannot leave us.”


    3. I asked, “Where will I stay?” They said, “You will sleep with us as a brother, not as a husband.
    You are our brother. From now on we will live with you, because we love you very much.” I was embarrassed
    to stay with them.


    4. The one who seemed to be first began kissing and embracing me.[b] The others saw her embrace me.
    They too began kissing me, leading me around the tower and playing with me.


    5. I felt as if I had become younger, and I too began playing with them. Some danced together, some
    danced, and some sang.[c] I walked silently with them around the tower and was glad to be with them.


    6. That evening I wanted to go home, but they kept me there. I stayed with them that night and slept
    beside the tower.


    7. They spread their linen tunics on the ground and had me lie down among them. They did nothing except
    pray. I prayed with them continually, no less than they did. They were glad to see me pray like this.
    I stayed with them until the second hour of the next day.[d]


    8. Then the shepherd came. He asked the virgins, “Have you done him any harm?” They said, “Ask him.”
    I said, “Sir, I was glad to stay with them.” He asked, “What did you have for supper?” I said, “Sir,
    I feasted on the Lord’s words all night.” He asked, “Did they receive you well?” I said, “Yes, sir.”


    9. He asked, “What do you want to hear first?” I said, “Sir, just as you showed me things from the
    beginning, I ask you to explain them to me as I ask you questions.” He said, “As you wish. I will
    explain it and hide nothing from you.”'

base_translation:
  text: 'The virgins said to me, “The shepherd is not coming here today.” “What, then, shall I do?” I
    said. “Wait for him until late,” they said.[a] “If he comes, he will speak with you. If he does not
    come, you will stay here with us until he comes.”


    2. I said to them, “I will wait for him until late. But if he does not come, I will go home and return
    in the morning.” They replied, “You have been entrusted to us. You cannot leave us.”


    3. “Where, then, will I stay?” I said. “You will sleep with us as a brother, not as a husband,” they
    said. “You are our brother, and from now on we are going to live with you, for we love you very much.”
    I was embarrassed to stay with them.


    4. The one who seemed to be first among them began kissing and embracing me.[b] When the others saw
    her embracing me, they too began kissing me, leading me around the tower and playing with me.


    5. I felt as though I had become younger, and I too began playing with them. Some danced in a chorus,
    others danced, and others sang.[c] I walked silently with them around the tower and was glad to be
    with them.


    6. When evening came, I wanted to go home. But they would not let me; they kept me there. I stayed
    with them that night and slept beside the tower.


    7. The virgins spread their linen tunics on the ground and had me lie down in their midst. They did
    nothing at all except pray. I too prayed with them continually, no less than they did. The virgins
    rejoiced to see me praying like this. I remained there with them until the second hour of the next
    day.[d]


    8. Then the shepherd arrived and said to the virgins, “Have you done him any harm?” “Ask him,” they
    said. I said to him, “Sir, I was glad to stay with them.” “What did you have for supper?” he said.
    “Sir,” I said, “I feasted on the Lord’s words all night.” “Did they receive you well?” he said. “Yes,
    sir,” I said.


    9. “Now,” he said, “what do you want to hear first?” “Sir,” I said, “just as you showed me things
    from the beginning, I ask you to explain them as I ask you about them.” “As you wish,” he said. “I
    will explain them to you and hide nothing at all from you.”'
